correctness.rationale: In logit coordinates the derivative of the return map is exp(∫a x(1−x)dt)>1, and the displacement has opposite limiting signs; thus the unique interior fixed point is repelling and separates the pure-state basins. On that orbit h1<ell<u<h2, ascent and descent traverse the same interval, and the weighted residence density w is the sum of the two reciprocal phase velocities after removing a_i. Its mass is abar T and its first moment is abar hT by integrating the logit drift. Differentiating these two moments gives w(u)u'=abar(h−ell)/(u−ell) and −w(ell)ell'=abar(u−h)/(u−ell), establishing endpoint order and (TV)'=(h−ell)(u−h). The expectation of (x−ell)(u−x) is strictly positive, so TV'>0. The logit and frequency fixed-point multipliers agree by conjugacy, and the weighted mean gives Lambda=abar[h(1−h)−V]. For small T the width is O(T); smooth positive w near h makes the midpoint differ from h by O(T²), and the first phase then gives width vT+O(T²). The normalized smooth density differs relatively from uniform by O(T), giving the variance coefficient v²/12. For large T the divergent ascent and descent times force ell→h1 and u→h2 respectively, and averaging (TV)' gives the asserted limit. Its positivity is the selection-weighted average of h_i(1−h_i) multiplied by abar. Independently at (a1,a2,h1,h2,p,T)=(3,3,1/3,2/3,1/2,12), symmetry and bisection on the elementary ascent-time integral give ell=0.33814357714 and u=0.66185642286. Integrating 1/(x−h1)+1/(h2−x) from ell to u and dividing by T gives Lambda=0.70397655882, and the identity gives V=0.01534114706.
residual_risks: The numerical agreement tests one case only. The theorem uses fixed duty fraction and payoff parameters and the per-unit-time exponent, not monotone decrease of the raw multiplier or any conclusion about feedback or higher-dimensional systems.

value.rationale: The residence derivative resolves the direction of a natural switching-timescale comparison that uniqueness and repulsion cannot answer. Its connection to strict variance growth identifies how the orbit widens while weakening the repulsion per unit time and yields both limiting rates; this is a structural quantitative result rather than another oscillating example.
residual_risks: The derivative concerns an exceptional orbit in a precommitted scalar model, not robustness of interior coexistence in arbitrary games.
